title: Uncertain herbal anchor on f9v with wild pansy as the picture candidate
sources: P. Han (2011), Discussion of the plant illustrated in folio f9v of the Voynich Manuscript, https://www.as.up.krakow.pl/jvs/library/2-7-2011-05-25/pansyvm.pdf.
Siv Bugge Vatne (2022), The morphology of the Voynich plants, https://crackingthevoynichcipher.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/5_the_morphology_of_the_voynich_plants_siv_bugge_vatne_2022.pdf.
René Zandbergen's index of early tentative identifications gives the f9v entry from Petersen's manuscript notes and its reported attribution to O'Neill, https://www.voynich.nu/extra/herb_oldid.html.
statement: Han and Vatne each favor wild pansy (Viola tricolor) in published discussions and compare f9v with the same Lindman botanical plate. Han also photographs a modern garden pansy and demonstrates a flattening hypothesis for the apparently inverted broad petal. Vatne notes the petal orientation and emphasizes the two forms of green appendages and the branching habit. On the Beinecke scan I see five-part flowers, one broad petal facing upward in the upper right blossom, blue and pale tones, broad basal leaves, deeply divided green appendages above, and a fibrous root. These are reasons to retain Viola as an illustration candidate. Species specificity and the cause of the petal orientation remain open. The text in this area appears as paragraphs that wrap around the flowers. I found no stand-alone Voynich token with a clear pointing relationship to the plant. In the pinned ZL 3b transliteration fochor begins the first prose line at f9v.1. Treating it as the plant name would need separate evidence. The candidate here is for the illustration and the word and name fields are empty.
